To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the choice of gene matching method is very important in improving cross-platform data consistency and that (2) the use of exon-based gene matching, combined with stringent data preprocessing, can lead to good consistency across platforms, and that (3) commercial arrays were generally more consistent than " in-house" arrays, while one-dye platforms are more consistent than two dye platforms.

(i) exon-based probe sequence matching improves cross-platform data consistency; (ii) the consistency is good for high-expression genes; (iii) the consistency is variable for low-expression genes; (iv) commercial platforms are more consistent than "home-made" platforms; and (v) one-dye platforms are more consistent that two-dye platforms
(a) probe sequence-based matching at the exon level improves consistency of data from different platforms and (b) commercial one-dye platforms are the most consistent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic comparison of microarray platforms, which is a necessary step for the application of multiple platforms in a single study.
the general problem of cross-platform data consistency, and the framework developed is a general tool for systematic comparisons of microarray data across platforms.
the practical issues of cross-platform data comparisons, which are important for many applications in genomics research, including data integration, meta-analysis and data sharing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the consistency of cross-platform data is highly dependent on both the experimental conditions and the data preprocessing protocols, and it is important to consider these factors in cross-platform comparisons.
, for the platforms we studied, the best cross-platform data consistency is obtained by using the same platform, and by using a one-dye platform.
the choice of the platform should depend on the specific research question, and the data consistency of the platform should be considered in addition to other factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the most part, gene expression data generated from different microarray platforms are highly comparable, and the consistency is good enough for most applications

for the platforms studied, the one-dye Affymetrix U133A platform was most consistent, followed by the two-dye Illumina HumanHT-12 v4.0 platform, and then by the two-dyes Illumina HumanWG-6 v3.0, the two-dye Agilent 60K, the two-dyes Agilent 1M, and the one-dye Agilent G4112A.
for a given experiment, it is possible to find a platform that would provide good data quality, but it is important to consider the trade-offs between platform performance and experimental design
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while it is possible to compare microarray data from different platforms, it is very difficult to do it with high confidence.
the quality of microarray data can be greatly enhanced by careful experimental design, data processing, and cross-platform gene matching.
, while there are some limitations, it is possible to compare data from diverse platforms, and to use these comparisons to improve our understanding of microarray technology.
